nodes.languageNotes: Uses go-jose v4 with HS256 and a runtime-reloadable HMAC key.

nodes.name: NewJWTSigner
nodes.summary: Constructs an HS256 JOSE signer backed by a hot-reloadable HMAC key; shared between WFE2 (mint) and SFE (verify) to keep unpause tokens interoperable.

nodes.name: JWTClaims
nodes.summary: Boulder-specific unpause JWT claim set embedding jwt.Claims plus API version (V) and comma-joined paused identifiers (I); used to scope an unpause action to a specific account and identifier list.

nodes.name: GenerateJWT
nodes.summary: WFE2 mints an unpause JWT for regID+identifiers with bounded lifetime and Boulder issuer/audience claims; serialized token is embedded in the pause-notification email link to the SFE.

nodes.name: RedeemJWT
nodes.summary: SFE-side validator: parses and verifies the unpause JWT's signature, issuer, audience, API version, and expiry (allowing one minute of clock skew) before handing control off to the RA to unpause identifiers.

nodes.name: va/caa.go
nodes.summary: CAA rechecking for the Validation Authority: DoCAA gRPC entry point, recursive CAA tree-climb lookups, record parsing (issue/issuewild/iodef/validationmethods/accountURI), MPIC-aware fan-out to remote VAs, and metrics.
nodes.languageNotes: Primary VA logs and observes latency on both local and primary+remote axes.

nodes.name: DoCAA
nodes.summary: gRPC handler implementing the CAA.DoCAA RPC: the primary VA runs a local CAA check then fans out to remote VAs via doRemoteOperation to meet MPIC corroboration requirements; remote VAs only do the local check.

nodes.name: checkCAA
nodes.summary: Orchestrates CAA evaluation for one identifier: calls checkCAARecords to climb the CAA tree and audit-logs the result; wraps DNS errors in berrors.DNSError and policy failures in berrors.CAAError.

nodes.name: filterCAA
nodes.summary: Partitions raw CAA RRs into issue/issuewild buckets and flags unknown critical directives that force unauthorized per RFC 8659.

nodes.name: parallelCAALookup
nodes.summary: Concurrently queries CAA for every ancestor label of the target name via bdns; returns per-label caaResult records so selectCAA can pick the closest non-empty set.

nodes.name: selectCAA
nodes.summary: Chooses the closest-ancestor caaResult that has records or errors, implementing the CAA lookup algorithm from RFC 8659 Section 3.

nodes.name: getCAA
nodes.summary: Driver that builds the label list from a hostname, invokes parallelCAALookup, and selects the authoritative record set for validateCAA to evaluate.

nodes.name: checkCAARecords
nodes.summary: Normalizes the identifier, strips an optional wildcard label, fetches CAA via getCAA, and evaluates via validateCAA; returns whether CAA was present and a free-form response summary for audit logs.

nodes.name: validateCAA
nodes.summary: Applies Boulder's issue/issuewild policy to a CAA set: enforces the unknown-critical flag, picks issue vs issuewild based on wildcard context, matches issuer domain, optional accountURI, and validationmethods parameters, and emits authorized/unauthorized metrics.

nodes.name: parseCAARecord
nodes.summary: Parses a single CAA issue/issuewild value into the issuer domain plus tag=value parameters, rejecting duplicates and malformed tokens per RFC 8657.

nodes.name: caaAccountURIMatches
nodes.summary: Enforces the RFC 8657 accounturi CAA parameter by matching the record value against Boulder's configured account URI prefixes plus the subscriber's account ID.

nodes.name: caaValidationMethodMatches
nodes.summary: Enforces the RFC 8657 validationmethods CAA parameter by checking the ACME challenge type against a comma-separated allowlist, validating token syntax and known challenge names.

nodes.name: va/config/config.go
nodes.summary: Shared Common VA config struct (DNS provider/timeouts, issuer domain, user agent, account URI prefixes) reused by boulder-va and boulder-remoteva cmd binaries; provides SetDefaultsAndValidate for their bootstrap paths.

nodes.name: Common
nodes.summary: VA configuration shared by the primary boulder-va and boulder-remoteva processes: DNS resolver settings (tries, provider, static resolvers, timeout, loopback), issuer domain, user agent, and ACME account URI prefixes for CAA validation.

nodes.name: SetDefaultsAndValidate
nodes.summary: Validates that the VA cmd has grpc and debug listen addresses; used by boulder-va/boulder-remoteva bootstrap before wiring gRPC servers.

nodes.name: va/dns.go
nodes.summary: DNS plumbing for the Validation Authority: resolves A/AAAA for HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN-01 (filtering IANA-reserved addresses) and implements the DNS-01 and DNS-ACCOUNT-01 challenge validators via TXT lookup under the _acme-challenge label.

nodes.name: getAddrs
nodes.summary: Runs parallel A and AAAA lookups via bdns, drops reserved/link-local addresses (unless allowRestrictedAddrs), and returns usable IPs plus resolver identity for HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN-01 dialing.

nodes.name: availableAddresses
nodes.summary: Partitions a resolved address list into IPv4 and IPv6 buckets so processHTTPValidation/tryGetChallengeCert can prefer v6 with v4 fallback per Boulder's MPIC dialing policy.

nodes.name: validateDNSAccount01
nodes.summary: Implements the draft-ietf-acme-dns-account-label DNS-ACCOUNT-01 challenge: derives the account-scoped label prefix from SHA-256(accountURI) base32, then delegates to validateDNS for TXT comparison.

nodes.name: validateDNS
nodes.summary: Shared backbone for DNS-01/DNS-ACCOUNT-01: looks up TXT records under the challenge prefix, constant-time matches against SHA-256 of the key authorization, and reports found values on mismatch for debuggability.

nodes.name: va/dns_persist.go
nodes.summary: Implementation of Boulder's draft DNS-PERSIST-01 challenge: validates a long-lived _acme-persist TXT record (issuer, accountURI, policy, persistUntil) against a previously validated authorization, enabling CAA-like proof-of-control persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated by the DNSPersist01 feature flag in va.go.

nodes.name: parseDNSPersistRecord
nodes.summary: Parses a _acme-persist TXT record into issuer + tag/value params (accountURI, policy, persistUntil), enforcing tag uniqueness, whitespace rules, and that the issuer matches Boulder's configured issuerDomain.

nodes.name: checkDNSPersistRecord
nodes.summary: Policy check for a parsed persist record: requires accountURI match, wildcard policy (when the authz is for a wildcard), and that validatedAt falls before persistUntil.

nodes.name: validateDNSPersist01
nodes.summary: DNS-PERSIST-01 validator: fetches _acme-persist TXT records, parses each one, and returns success if any matches Boulder's issuer, the caller's accountURI, and an unexpired persistUntil; collects parse errors for diagnostic reporting.

nodes.name: va/http.go
nodes.summary: HTTP-01 challenge validator: pre-resolved-IP dialer, IPv6-then-IPv4 fallback, redirect target validation (scheme/port/host/IP-literal/TLD rules), body length limits, and UTF-8-safe response handling — all enforcing Boulder's anti-SSRF reserved-IP checks.

nodes.name: DialContext
nodes.summary: preresolvedDialer hook that forces net/http to connect to the VA-chosen IP:port, enforces a per-attempt singleDialTimeout, and refuses mismatched host dials (rejecting follow-up CONNECTs to arbitrary redirect targets).

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: error interface implementation for dialerMismatchError — used when net/http tries to dial a host that differs from the preresolvedDialer's target, signaling the VA to fail closed.

nodes.name: httpTransport
nodes.summary: Builds a net/http.Transport with TLS validation disabled (HTTP-01 uses plain HTTP; TLS only happens during redirects where identity is policed separately), using the preresolvedDialer for both HTTP and HTTPS dials.

nodes.name: httpValidationTarget
nodes.summary: State for an HTTP-01 attempt: chosen host/port/path/query, v6/v4 address queues with nextIP cursor, and the resolver that returned each address; tracks which IPs have been tried for fallback/validation-record emission.

nodes.name: nextIP
nodes.summary: Advances an httpValidationTarget to its next available IP (record it in tried and set cur); the key fallback hook when an initial IPv6 HTTP-01 attempt fails with a network error.

nodes.name: newHTTPValidationTarget
nodes.summary: Constructs an httpValidationTarget for a DNS or IP identifier: reuses IP identifier addresses verbatim or resolves via getAddrs, splits into v6/v4 queues, and rejects when no usable addresses remain.

nodes.name: extractRequestTarget
nodes.summary: Validates redirect URLs for HTTP-01: enforces http/https scheme, allowed ports (httpPort/httpsPort/TLSPort), strips userinfo, rejects trailing-dot hosts, resolves IP literals against the reserved-IP checker, and chooses DNS vs IP identifier for the next hop.

nodes.name: setupHTTPValidation
nodes.summary: Wires the current httpValidationTarget into the outgoing request: rewrites URL to the selected IP, enforces reserved-IP policy, attaches a preresolvedDialer, and records the address in the challenge ValidationRecord.

nodes.name: fallbackErr
nodes.summary: Classifies a transport error as eligible for IPv6→IPv4 fallback: syscall-level connection errors trigger another nextIP attempt, anything else is treated as a final failure.

nodes.name: processHTTPValidation
nodes.summary: Core HTTP-01 driver: builds request, dials via preresolvedDialer, follows up to kMaxRedirect redirects (each re-validated through extractRequestTarget + setupHTTPValidation), enforces IPv6→IPv4 fallback, limits body size, and returns response bytes plus the ordered ValidationRecord trail.

nodes.name: validateHTTP01
nodes.summary: HTTP-01 entry point: GETs /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token>, trims RFC5234-WSP, and constant-time compares the body to the expected key authorization.

nodes.name: va.proto
nodes.summary: gRPC schema for the Validation Authority: VA.DoDCV (domain control validation) and CAA.DoCAA RPCs, with IsCAAValid/PerformValidation request/response messages carrying perspective and RIR fields that carry MPIC provenance from remote VAs back to the primary VA.

nodes.name: va/tlsalpn.go
nodes.summary: TLS-ALPN-01 challenge validator per RFC 8737: dials the subscriber with the acme-tls/1 ALPN, demands a self-signed challenge cert whose SAN matches the identifier and whose id-pe-acmeIdentifier extension contains SHA-256(keyAuthorization).

nodes.name: certAltNames
nodes.summary: Collects all SAN values (DNS, IP, email, URI) from an x509.Certificate into a normalized, deduplicated list used to craft error messages when TLS-ALPN-01 SAN checks fail.

nodes.name: tryGetChallengeCert
nodes.summary: Resolves the identifier, prefers IPv6 on the configured TLS port, falls back to IPv4 with tlsALPN-specific metrics, and delegates per-IP connection attempts to getChallengeCert.

nodes.name: getChallengeCert
nodes.summary: Dials the target hostPort with NextProtos=["acme-tls/1"] and InsecureSkipVerify, captures the peer certificate, enforces at least one cert in the chain, and returns the leaf for ALPN extension/SAN checking.

nodes.name: checkExpectedSAN
nodes.summary: Ensures the challenge cert has exactly one SAN matching the identifier (DNS or IP encoded per RFC 5280), rejecting multi-SAN or mismatched certs that could be used for ALPN confusion attacks.

nodes.name: checkAcceptableExtensions
nodes.summary: Whitelists x509 extensions allowed in a TLS-ALPN-01 cert: id-pe-acmeIdentifier (required) plus id-ce-subjectAltName, rejecting anything else per RFC 8737 Section 3.

nodes.name: validateTLSALPN01
nodes.summary: TLS-ALPN-01 entry point: obtains the challenge cert, verifies self-signature, checks allowed extensions, SAN match, and that the id-pe-acmeIdentifier extension carries the critical flag and a SHA-256(keyAuth) octet-string payload.

nodes.name: va/utf8filter.go
nodes.summary: Sanitizer that replaces invalid UTF-8 sequences in VA problem details before they are returned over gRPC or rendered to ACME clients, since protobuf string fields and the ACME problem+json type must be UTF-8.

nodes.name: replaceInvalidUTF8
nodes.summary: Rewrites a byte slice by replacing invalid UTF-8 runes with U+FFFD so validation error strings stay protobuf-safe even when the challenge target returned garbage bytes.

nodes.name: filterProblemDetails
nodes.summary: Returns a probs.ProblemDetails copy with the Type and Detail fields scrubbed via replaceInvalidUTF8 — called on every DoDCV/DoCAA return path before the result is sent to the RA.

nodes.name: va.go
nodes.summary: Core Validation Authority: ValidationAuthorityImpl type, metrics, remote-VA fan-out with MPIC quorum and RIR diversity, experimental-VA shadow mode, challenge dispatcher (HTTP-01/DNS-01/DNS-ACCOUNT-01/DNS-PERSIST-01/TLS-ALPN-01), detailedError classifier, and the VA.DoDCV gRPC entry point.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements ACME domain control validation entry point and MPIC corroboration orchestration.

nodes.name: RemoteClients
nodes.summary: Composite gRPC client type combining the VA and CAA client stubs used to call a remote VA; one instance per remote VA address.

nodes.name: RemoteVA
nodes.summary: Bundles a RemoteClients stub with its Address, Perspective (e.g., datacenter label), and RIR (e.g., ARIN/RIPE) — the key data Boulder uses to enforce MPIC corroboration diversity across at least two RIRs.

nodes.name: vaMetrics
nodes.summary: Prometheus metric bundle: validation latency histogram, CAA failure/outcome counters, TLS-ALPN OID counter, HTTP-01 redirect and fallback counters, IPv4-fallback counter, and experimental-VA concurrence gauge.

nodes.name: ValidationAuthorityImpl
nodes.summary: gRPC server struct for the VA: holds dnsClient, logger, clock, remoteVAs slice, MPIC perspective/RIR identity, account URI prefixes, dial timeouts, reserved-IP checker, experimental-VA config, and metrics; implements the VA.DoDCV and CAA.DoCAA RPCs.

nodes.name: mpicSummary
nodes.summary: Human-readable MPIC corroboration summary emitted to audit logs: which perspectives passed, which failed, how many distinct RIRs among passers, and a final quorum verdict string.

nodes.name: validationLogEvent
nodes.summary: Per-DoDCV audit log event structure: AuthzID, Requester account, Identifier, Challenge snapshot, Error, InternalError, Latency, and the MPIC Summary string.

nodes.name: initMetrics
nodes.summary: Registers all VA Prometheus metrics against the shared registerer, including validation latency histogram with (operation, perspective, challenge_type, problem_type, result) labels.

nodes.name: NewValidationAuthorityImpl
nodes.summary: Constructor: validates that every RemoteVA has an Address, Perspective, and RIR; normalizes the issuer domain; wires metrics and dial timeouts; computes maxRemoteFailures from the MPIC quorum rule; stores the optional experimental-VA and its sample rate.

nodes.name: runExperiment
nodes.summary: Runs the experimental-VA in shadow mode under a bounded timeout and a WithoutCancel context, compares its result against the primary result, increments the concurrence counter, and audit-logs divergences without affecting the subscriber outcome.

nodes.name: Unwrap
nodes.summary: ipError Unwrap: exposes the underlying network or protocol error so errors.As/Is can still classify it when a per-IP error is wrapped for ValidationRecord emission.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: ipError string format: prefixes the wrapped error with the IP that generated it so HTTP-01/TLS-ALPN-01 per-address failures remain attributable in logs and ACME problem details.

nodes.name: detailedError
nodes.summary: Classifier that converts low-level Go errors (tls.Alert, tls.RecordHeaderError, net.OpError, syscall errnos, context.Canceled, berrors types) into ACME probs.ProblemDetails with appropriate URN types (connection, tls, dns, unauthorized, malformed, caa).

nodes.name: validateChallenge
nodes.summary: Dispatches to the challenge-specific validator based on core.AcmeChallenge kind, gating DNS-ACCOUNT-01 and DNS-PERSIST-01 behind the DNSAccount01 / DNSPersist01 feature flags.

nodes.name: observeLatency
nodes.summary: Single call that records the validation-latency histogram with operation, perspective (primary|remote|all), challenge type, problem type, and outcome labels.

nodes.name: summarizeMPIC
nodes.summary: Builds an mpicSummary from remote-VA responses: sorts passed/failed perspective lists, collects the set of RIRs among passers, and produces a human-readable quorum verdict for audit logs.

nodes.name: doRemoteOperation
nodes.summary: Parallel fan-out to remote VAs: issues op per RemoteVA under a shared context, validates that each response's Perspective/RIR matches the expected remote, applies the MPIC quorum rule (fail if too many failures, else run an optional slow-remote timer), and returns a combined probs.ProblemDetails + mpicSummary.

nodes.name: DoDCV
nodes.summary: gRPC entry point for ACME domain control validation: on the primary VA runs the local challenge via validateChallenge then fans out to remote VAs through doRemoteOperation, enforcing MPIC corroboration; on a remote VA only the local validation runs. Emits an audit log event with perspective, latency, and MPIC summary.

nodes.name: web/context.go
nodes.summary: HTTP request context plumbing for Boulder's WFE2. Defines RequestEvent (per-request ACME log record) and TopHandler, the outermost HTTP middleware that wraps every ACME handler to capture timing, status, errors, real IP, UA, and structured audit logging.

nodes.name: RequestEvent
nodes.summary: Structured record of a single ACME HTTP request: endpoint, requester account, status, latency, slug, identifiers, challenge type, errors. Emitted as the per-request JSON audit log line.

nodes.name: TopHandler
nodes.summary: Outermost HTTP middleware wrapping every WFE2 ACME handler. Populates RequestEvent, enforces timeouts, and logs the request after the inner handler completes.

nodes.name: wfeHandler
nodes.summary: Function-type adapter that lets WFE2 methods with the (ctx, logEvent, response, request) signature satisfy http.Handler via ServeHTTP.

nodes.name: responseWriterWithStatus
nodes.summary: http.ResponseWriter wrapper that captures the status code so TopHandler can record it in the RequestEvent.

nodes.name: UserAgent
nodes.summary: Retrieves the User-Agent stashed in the request context by the WFE2 middleware.

nodes.name: WithUserAgent
nodes.summary: Stores the request's User-Agent into the context so downstream ACME handlers can log it.

nodes.name: NewTopHandler
nodes.summary: Constructs the top-level WFE2 HTTP middleware that wraps each ACME endpoint with logging and request bookkeeping.

nodes.name: TopHandler.ServeHTTP
nodes.summary: Per-request entry point for every WFE2 ACME endpoint. Sets up the RequestEvent, calls the inner handler, and emits the final JSON audit log line with status, latency, and errors.

nodes.name: KeyTypeToString
nodes.summary: Formats an account public key's algorithm/curve/bit size for audit logging of ACME account and key rollover events.

nodes.name: web/docs.go
nodes.summary: Package doc comment for web/, describing shared HTTP helpers used by Boulder's WFE2 ACME server.

nodes.name: web/extract.go
nodes.summary: Helper that extracts the real client IP for ACME requests, preferring the trusted X-Real-IP header set by Boulder's front-end load balancer.

nodes.name: ExtractRequesterIP
nodes.summary: Returns the real client IP of an ACME request, using X-Real-IP if present and falling back to RemoteAddr.

nodes.name: web/probs.go
nodes.summary: Maps Boulder internal error types (berrors) to RFC 8555 ACME problem documents with the correct urn:ietf:params:acme:error:* types and HTTP statuses.

nodes.name: problemDetailsForBoulderError
nodes.summary: Translates a single berrors.BoulderError into an ACME ProblemDetails with the appropriate ACME problem type and HTTP status (malformed, unauthorized, rateLimited, caa, dns, badNonce, etc.).

nodes.name: ProblemDetailsForError
nodes.summary: Public entry point used by WFE2 to turn any error into an ACME ProblemDetails document, collecting subproblems from a BoulderError's sub-errors.

nodes.name: web/relative.go
nodes.summary: Builds fully-qualified ACME URLs from a request + relative path, honoring the X-Forwarded-Proto header behind Boulder's TLS-terminating load balancer.

nodes.name: RelativeEndpoint
nodes.summary: Composes an absolute URL for an ACME endpoint (Location/Link headers, directory) from the request host and a relative path.

nodes.name: web/send_error.go
nodes.summary: Shared helper that writes an ACME ProblemDetails JSON error response, records it on the RequestEvent, and logs internal errors distinctly from user-visible ones.

nodes.name: SendError
nodes.summary: Writes an ACME Problem JSON response with the correct Content-Type and status, appends user/internal errors to the RequestEvent, and suppresses log output for expected 4xx responses.

nodes.name: web/server.go
nodes.summary: Small wrapper around net/http.Server that routes stdlib error output through Boulder's structured logger. Used by the WFE2 daemon as the HTTP server base.

nodes.name: errorWriter
nodes.summary: io.Writer that forwards net/http internal error log lines to Boulder's blog.Logger so they end up in the structured audit log.

nodes.name: NewServer
nodes.summary: Builds an *http.Server preconfigured to log stdlib errors through Boulder's logger; used by the WFE2 daemon.

nodes.name: wfe2/README.md
nodes.summary: Short README for the wfe2 package describing its role as Boulder's RFC 8555 ACME front-end (the 'v2' Web Front End).

nodes.name: wfe2/cache.go
nodes.summary: In-process TTL cache wrapping the SA's GetRegistration so WFE2 does not hit the database on every authenticated ACME request. Degrades gracefully to direct SA lookups when the cache is disabled.

nodes.name: AccountGetter
nodes.summary: Interface abstracting 'fetch an ACME registration by regID'. Implemented both by the SA gRPC client and by accountCache, letting WFE2 swap in a cached lookup.

nodes.name: accountCache
nodes.summary: Bounded TTL cache of ACME registrations keyed by account ID, used by WFE2 to avoid an SA round-trip on every JWS-authenticated request.

nodes.name: NewAccountCache
nodes.summary: Constructs an accountCache with the given SA backend, entry cap, TTL, and clock; wires a Prometheus counter for cache hits/misses.

nodes.name: accountCache.GetRegistration
nodes.summary: Cache-aware registration lookup: serves fresh entries from memory, otherwise queries the SA and populates the cache. Emits 'hit'/'miss' metrics.

nodes.name: wfe2/stats.go
nodes.summary: Prometheus metrics for WFE2: HTTP error counts, JOSE verification failures, observed CSR signature algorithms, malformed EC points, nonce backend mismatches, and ARI replacement order counts.

nodes.name: wfe2Stats
nodes.summary: Struct holding all Prometheus collectors exported by the WFE2 process.

nodes.name: initStats
nodes.summary: Registers WFE2's Prometheus collectors (http_error_count, jose_error_count, csr_signature_algs, etc.) with the given registry and returns the wfe2Stats bundle.

nodes.name: wfe2/verify.go
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 JWS verification for every authenticated ACME request. Parses flattened JWS bodies, enforces supported algorithms, validates nonces against the nonce service, checks the JWS url header matches the request URL, resolves account keys (embedded vs kid), and performs the double-JWS dance for account key rollover.

nodes.name: sigAlgorithmForKey
nodes.summary: Maps an account public key to the single JWS signature algorithm Boulder accepts for it (RS256, ES256/384/512).

nodes.name: checkAlgorithm
nodes.summary: Rejects JWS using algorithms that do not match the account key or that Boulder has explicitly disallowed.

nodes.name: enforceJWSAuthType
nodes.summary: Asserts a parsed JWS is either embedded-JWK or kid-authenticated as required by the specific ACME endpoint.

nodes.name: validPOSTRequest
nodes.summary: Sanity-checks that an ACME POST body is a well-formed JWS HTTP request (method, Content-Type, non-empty body).

nodes.name: nonceWellFormed
nodes.summary: Validates that the nonce header value matches the expected base64 shape and prefix length before calling the nonce service.

nodes.name: validNonce
nodes.summary: Calls the nonce service (via the gRPC nonce balancer) to verify and consume the anti-replay nonce on an ACME JWS.

nodes.name: validPOSTURL
nodes.summary: Ensures the JWS protected header's url matches the request URL, as required by RFC 8555 section 6.4.

nodes.name: matchJWSURLs
nodes.summary: Checks that an outer and inner JWS (used in key rollover) carry matching url headers.

nodes.name: parseJWS
nodes.summary: Parses a flattened JSON JWS from a request body, rejecting multi-signature and compact forms.

nodes.name: parseJWSRequest
nodes.summary: Reads the request body and returns the parsed JWS, recording body parse errors on the RequestEvent.

nodes.name: extractJWK
nodes.summary: Extracts and validates the embedded JWK from a jwk-authenticated JWS (used for new-account and revoke-by-cert-key).

nodes.name: acctIDFromURL
nodes.summary: Parses an ACME account URL into a numeric regID, enforcing Boulder's /acme/acct/N URL layout.

nodes.name: lookupJWK
nodes.summary: Resolves the account key referenced by a kid-authenticated JWS by looking up the registration through the SA/account cache.

nodes.name: validJWSForKey
nodes.summary: Verifies a JWS signature with a specific JWK and re-parses the inner payload as a JWS-authenticated ACME request.

nodes.name: validJWSForAccount
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper that looks up the account's key and verifies a kid-authenticated JWS in one call.

nodes.name: validPOSTForAccount
nodes.summary: Full validation pipeline for an authenticated ACME POST: parse JWS, check nonce/url, look up account, verify signature.

nodes.name: validPOSTAsGETForAccount
nodes.summary: Validates a POST-as-GET ACME request: like validPOSTForAccount but requires an empty payload per RFC 8555.

nodes.name: validSelfAuthenticatedJWS
nodes.summary: Verifies a JWS signed by its own embedded key (new-account, revoke-by-cert-key) and returns the key and payload.

nodes.name: validSelfAuthenticatedPOST
nodes.summary: End-to-end validation for self-authenticated POSTs including nonce and url checks and good-key policy enforcement.

nodes.name: validKeyRollover
nodes.summary: Validates an RFC 8555 key-rollover: outer JWS signed by the current account key, inner JWS signed by the new key, old/new keys cross-referenced.

nodes.name: wfe2/wfe.go
nodes.summary: Boulder's RFC 8555 ACME server implementation. Hosts every public ACME endpoint (directory, newNonce, newAccount, newOrder, newAuthz, orders, authz, challenge, finalize, cert, revoke-cert, key-change, renewalInfo), plus CORS handling, account cache integration, ARI replacement logic, rate limiting, and pause/unpause support. Backbone of the WFE2 daemon.

nodes.name: WebFrontEndImpl
nodes.summary: Concrete ACME front-end implementation. Holds RA/SA/EE/nonce gRPC clients, key policy, rate limiter, unpause signer, certificate profile policy, cached issuer chains, and hosts every ACME HTTP handler method. Assembled by the wfe2 daemon main.

nodes.name: orderJSON
nodes.summary: Over-the-wire representation of an ACME order as defined by RFC 8555 (status, expires, identifiers, authorizations, finalize URL, certificate URL, profile, error, replaces).

nodes.name: WfeHealthzResponse
nodes.summary: Response body for /healthz used by load balancers and the deployment pipeline to confirm the WFE2 can reach its RA and SA dependencies.

nodes.name: revocationEvidence
nodes.summary: Audit log record describing who revoked which certificate, why, and by which authentication method (subscriber key vs. cert key).

nodes.name: NewWebFrontEndImpl
nodes.summary: Constructor wiring the WFE2 with its RA/SA/EE gRPC clients, nonce service, rate limiter, key policy, issuer chains, certificate profile config, and unpause signer.

nodes.name: HandleFunc
nodes.summary: Registers a single ACME endpoint on the HTTP mux, attaching method allow-lists, CORS handling, and the standard middleware stack (TopHandler + JWS verification).

nodes.name: writeJsonResponse
nodes.summary: Serializes a value as JSON with the correct content type, updates the RequestEvent status, and writes it to the response.

nodes.name: relativeDirectory
nodes.summary: Rewrites the static ACME directory payload with the current request's scheme and host for correct Location/finalize URLs.

nodes.name: Handler
nodes.summary: Builds the WFE2's ServeMux, registering every ACME endpoint with HandleFunc. The HTTP entry point invoked by the daemon's main.

nodes.name: Index
nodes.summary: Handles GET / by returning a human-readable directory pointer and banning directory indexing of unknown paths.

nodes.name: Directory
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /directory endpoint: returns URLs for newNonce, newAccount, newOrder, revokeCert, keyChange, renewalInfo, and meta fields (caaIdentities, termsOfService, profiles).

nodes.name: Nonce
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/new-nonce endpoint: pulls a fresh anti-replay nonce from the nonce service and returns it via Replay-Nonce header.

nodes.name: sendError
nodes.summary: WFE2-level wrapper around web.SendError that also bumps the http_error_count Prometheus metric for the endpoint.

nodes.name: NewAccount
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/new-acct endpoint: validates a self-authenticated JWS, runs good-key policy, enforces new-account rate limits, creates the registration via the RA, and returns the Account JSON.

nodes.name: parseRevocation
nodes.summary: Parses a revoke-cert request payload: decodes the DER certificate, validates reason code, and looks up issuance metadata for audit.

nodes.name: revokeCertBySubscriberKey
nodes.summary: Revoke-cert path for an authenticated account that owns the certificate. Verifies ownership against the SA and calls the RA to revoke.

nodes.name: revokeCertByCertKey
nodes.summary: Revoke-cert path authenticated by signing with the certificate's own key (used for key-compromise revocations). Forces reason=keyCompromise and blocks the key via the RA.

nodes.name: RevokeCertificate
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/revoke-cert endpoint: dispatches to subscriber-key or cert-key paths based on JWS auth type and logs a revocationEvidence audit record.

nodes.name: ChallengeHandler
nodes.summary: Router for /acme/chall-v3/{authzID}/{challID}: splits the URL and delegates to getChallenge (POST-as-GET) or postChallenge (initiation).

nodes.name: Challenge
nodes.summary: Per-challenge handler: loads the authorization from the SA, verifies ownership, and either returns current state or initiates validation via the RA.

nodes.name: prepChallengeForDisplay
nodes.summary: Rewrites a gRPC-level challenge into the RFC 8555 JSON shape, including url, validated, and status, and strips internal-only fields.

nodes.name: prepAuthorizationForDisplay
nodes.summary: Rewrites a gRPC authorization into the RFC 8555 JSON shape, attaching absolute challenge URLs.

nodes.name: getChallenge
nodes.summary: Returns the current JSON state of a single challenge for POST-as-GET polling.

nodes.name: postChallenge
nodes.summary: Accepts an ACME challenge-initiation POST, validating that the challenge is pending, and asks the RA to perform the validation (HTTP-01/DNS-01/TLS-ALPN-01).

nodes.name: Account
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/acct/{regID} endpoint: supports POST-as-GET fetch and account updates (contacts, deactivation) via updateAccount.

nodes.name: updateAccount
nodes.summary: Applies allowed mutations to an account: contact list, deactivation. Rejects disallowed field changes and returns the updated account.

nodes.name: deactivateAuthorization
nodes.summary: Handles 'status:deactivated' updates on an authorization, asking the RA to mark it deactivated.

nodes.name: AuthorizationHandler
nodes.summary: Router for /acme/authz-v3/{authzID}, validating the path shape and delegating to Authorization.

nodes.name: Authorization
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/authz endpoint: returns the authorization and its challenges, or processes a deactivation request.

nodes.name: CertificateInfo
nodes.summary: Returns alternate issuer chain information as a JSON header to drive Link: alternate chains on Certificate responses.

nodes.name: Certificate
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/cert/{serial} endpoint: serves PEM certificate chains to the subscriber, supports alternate chain selection via the URL suffix, and enforces account ownership.

nodes.name: BuildID
nodes.summary: Exposes Boulder's build ID on a debug endpoint for deploy verification.

nodes.name: Healthz
nodes.summary: Liveness/readiness probe: calls the RA and SA to confirm they respond and returns a JSON health payload.

nodes.name: Options
nodes.summary: Handles OPTIONS preflight requests for CORS on ACME endpoints.

nodes.name: setCORSHeaders
nodes.summary: Writes the Access-Control-* headers for Boulder's CORS policy on ACME responses.

nodes.name: KeyRollover
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/key-change endpoint: validates the outer+inner JWS pair with validKeyRollover, runs good-key on the new key, and tells the RA to update the account key.

nodes.name: orderToOrderJSON
nodes.summary: Converts an SA Order proto into the RFC 8555 orderJSON wire format, including authz URLs and finalize URL.

nodes.name: checkNewOrderLimits
nodes.summary: Spends rate-limit budget for a new-order request (per-account and per-identifier) and returns an error if exceeded.

nodes.name: orderMatchesReplacement
nodes.summary: Confirms that an ARI 'replaces' hint points at a certificate whose identifiers are a subset of the new order, to authorize the ARI rate-limit exception.

nodes.name: determineARIWindow
nodes.summary: Given a serial, asks the SA for the certificate's ARI renewal window and builds the renewalInfo response body.

nodes.name: validateReplacementOrder
nodes.summary: Validates an ARI replacement order's 'replaces' field: ensures the predecessor exists, is owned by the account, matches identifiers, and is not already replaced.

nodes.name: validateCertificateProfileName
nodes.summary: Checks that a requested certificate profile name is configured and permitted.

nodes.name: checkIdentifiersPaused
nodes.summary: Checks the SA for any paused identifiers in the order and, if found, returns an ACME error with a pause page URL signed by the unpause signer.

nodes.name: NewOrder
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/new-order endpoint: parses the order, validates identifiers/profile/replaces, enforces order/newOrdersPerAccount rate limits, checks recursive on-demand domain blocks, and asks the RA to create the order.

nodes.name: GetOrder
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/order/{acctID}/{orderID} endpoint: POST-as-GET fetch of an order's current state.

nodes.name: FinalizeOrder
nodes.summary: RFC 8555 /acme/finalize endpoint: validates the account owns the order, parses the CSR, enforces CSR constraints, and asks the RA to issue the certificate.

nodes.name: RenewalInfo
nodes.summary: draft-ietf-acme-ari /acme/renewalInfo endpoint: returns the suggested renewal window for a certificate serial.

nodes.name: looksLikeRecursiveOnDemandRequest
nodes.summary: Heuristic that blocks new-order requests whose identifier set looks like recursive on-demand wildcard abuse against blocked labels.

layers.name: Web Frontend
layers.description: Public ACME HTTP surface (wfe2/) and subscriber self-service UI (sfe/), plus the shared web/ helpers for ACME request handling, problem-document rendering, and HTTP middleware. Terminates subscriber traffic and forwards ACME operations to the RA.

layers.name: Orchestration (RA)
layers.description: Registration Authority — the central coordinator that receives ACME operations from WFE2, drives validation through the VA, persists state via the SA, requests signing from the CA, and hands issued certificates to the Publisher and CRL pipeline.

layers.name: Identifier Validation
layers.description: Validation Authority (va/) and remote-VA perspectives, the Boulder DNS client (bdns/) used for DNS-01 / CAA / DNSSEC checks, and IANA data tables (iana/) for TLD and special-use name enforcement. Performs HTTP-01, DNS-01, DNS-ACCOUNT-01, TLS-ALPN-01, and CAA validation.

layers.name: Certificate Issuance
layers.description: Certificate Authority (ca/) that talks to the HSM, the issuance/ certificate builder, precert/ pre-certificate handling, CSR checks (csr/, goodkey/), policy enforcement (policy/, ctpolicy/), and the zlint-backed linter/ that gates every issuance against BR and ecosystem profiles.

layers.name: Storage (SA + DB)
layers.description: Storage Authority gRPC service (sa/) over MariaDB, the db/ helpers (gorp wrappers, rollback guards, sharding), and the SQL schema itself — tables, constraints, and .proto definitions that fix Boulder's durable state model for registrations, authorizations, orders, certificates, and CRL shards.

layers.name: Publication & Revocation
layers.description: publisher/ (submits issued certificates to Certificate Transparency logs and enforces SCT policy) and crl/ (the CRL generation pipeline — updater, storer, checker — that produces sharded CRLs signed by the CA).

layers.name: Supporting Services
layers.description: Auxiliary services and cross-cutting policy engines: nonce/ (ACME replay-nonce service), observer/ (external probers), ratelimits/ (Redis-backed GCRA limiter), allowlist/, salesforce/email-exporter integration, unpause/ (WebAuthN-based pause lift), and revocation/ metadata.

layers.name: Binary Entry Points
layers.description: cmd/*/main.go binaries — one per service (boulder-wfe2, boulder-ra, boulder-va, boulder-ca, boulder-sa, boulder-publisher, boulder-observer, nonce-service, sfe, crl-updater/storer/checker, email-exporter, bad-key-revoker, cert-checker, log-validator, remoteva, reversed-hostname-checker, admin, ceremony) plus the shared cmd shell (config.go, registry.go, shell.go) that wires configuration, signal handling, and command registration.

layers.name: Shared Libraries
layers.description: High-fan-in foundation used by every Boulder service: core/ (domain types and interfaces), grpc/ (client/server plumbing and interceptors), log/, metrics/, errors/, probs/ (ACME problem docs), identifier/, features/ (feature flags), config/, redis/, and utility packages (must, strictyaml, pkcs11helpers, privatekey).

layers.name: Infrastructure & Ops
layers.description: Operator-facing assets: top-level Dockerfile/Containerfile and docker-compose manifests, Makefile, go.mod, .github/ CI workflows and issue templates, docs/ architecture and contributor guides, data/ email templates, and the project README — everything that builds, tests, ships, and documents Boulder but is not compiled into a service binary.

tour.title: Project overview and component map
tour.description: Start with Boulder's README, which sketches the seven-component architecture: WFE (the ACME HTTP surface), RA (the orchestrator), VA, CA, SA, Publisher, and the CRL Updater. Note the ASCII diagram showing Subscriber -> WFE -> RA -> {VA, SA, CA} -> Publisher/CRL. This same shape drives every step of the tour — each component is a separate gRPC service, split along security-trust boundaries so that internet-facing binaries (WFE, VA, Publisher, CRL Storer) can be compromised without exposing the signing CA. Also note that Boulder's durable state is exactly five ACME object types: accounts, authorizations, challenges, orders, certificates.

tour.title: Unified boulder binary and command dispatch
tour.description: Boulder ships as a single binary that dispatches to a sub-command by name (boulder-wfe2, boulder-ra, boulder-va, boulder-ca, boulder-sa, boulder-publisher, crl-updater, nonce-service, sfe, admin, ceremony). cmd/boulder/main.go is a tiny dispatcher — each real service registers itself with cmd.RegisterCommand during init(), and registry.go holds the command table. shell.go provides the shared lifecycle (config loading, signal handling, scope-bound logger and metrics), and config.go centralizes typed config structures (TLS, gRPC, DB DSN, Redis). Every binary you meet in later steps plugs into these three files.

languageLesson.title: Go init() and the unified-binary pattern
languageLesson.content: Each cmd/boulder-*/main.go file declares an init() function that calls cmd.RegisterCommand("boulder-wfe2", main). init() runs automatically when the package is imported, so cmd/boulder/main.go can import all sub-packages and then pick which main() to call based on os.Args[0] or the first argument. This lets Boulder ship one binary that behaves as many — the same pattern BusyBox uses. Reading any main.go in cmd/ from here forward, look for this init() registration first.

tour.title: Core domain types shared across every service
tour.description: core/ holds the Boulder-wide Go representations of ACME objects (Registration, Authorization, Challenge, Order, Certificate) in objects.go — these are what the SA persists and what every gRPC protobuf ultimately maps to. interfaces.go defines the Go interfaces each service (RA, SA, VA, CA, Publisher) must satisfy, which is how gRPC clients are made drop-in substitutable for in-process implementations. challenges.go encodes the ACME challenge types (http-01, dns-01, dns-account-01, tls-alpn-01) that the VA will later execute. Anywhere you see these types imported in the rest of the tour, this is where they originate.

languageLesson.title: Go interfaces as service contracts
languageLesson.content: Boulder uses Go interfaces (core/interfaces.go) as the contract between services. The RA depends on a CertificateAuthority interface, not a concrete type; at wire-up time the RA receives a gRPC client that satisfies that interface. This makes the same RA code work in unit tests (with mock implementations), in the all-in-one dev binary (with in-process calls), and in production (with real gRPC clients). When reading any ra/, ca/, va/, or publisher/ code, look for an interface in core/ that describes the remote side.

tour.title: Web Front End — the ACME HTTP surface
tour.description: wfe2/wfe.go terminates subscriber HTTPS, implements the ACME endpoints (new-nonce, new-account, new-order, authz, challenge, finalize, cert, revoke-cert) and forwards each to the RA over gRPC. verify.go parses and cryptographically verifies the JWS envelope that wraps every authenticated ACME request, checking the signature against the registered account key or (for new-account) against the embedded JWK. The web/ package holds shared HTTP-level helpers: context.go attaches per-request state, probs.go renders ACME problem+json error documents, and send_error.go maps Go errors to the correct HTTP status plus problem type. The WFE is the only component the subscriber ever speaks to directly.

tour.title: Registration Authority — the orchestrator
tour.description: ra/ra.go receives each ACME operation from the WFE and sequences the calls to every other service: it asks the SA to create an order, the VA to perform challenge validation, the CA to issue, the Publisher to log, and the SA again to persist. ra/proto/ra.proto is the gRPC schema that fixes this API and is also the authoritative service contract — the generated ra.pb.go (excluded from this graph) is regenerated by `go generate`. The RA is also the enforcement point for rate limits and policy checks before issuance. If you are tracing an ACME flow end to end, start in the WFE and immediately follow the call into ra.go.

languageLesson.title: Protobuf service definitions
languageLesson.content: A .proto file defines messages (data shapes) and services (RPC methods). `service RegistrationAuthority { rpc NewOrder(NewOrderRequest) returns (Order) }` generates both a Go client and a Go server interface when protoc runs. Boulder commits the .proto as the source of truth and regenerates .pb.go with `go generate`; the generated files are deliberately excluded from this knowledge graph. When you want to know the full RA API surface, read ra.proto — not ra.go.

tour.title: Storage Authority — the durable state boundary
tour.description: sa/sa.go is the read-write gRPC server and saro.go is a read-only variant used by components that must never mutate state. sa.proto declares the full storage API: Add/Get/Update for registrations, authorizations, orders, certificates, plus revocation and CRL-shard bookkeeping. sa/db/01-boulder_sa.sql is the authoritative MariaDB schema — tables for registrations, authz2, orders, certificates, certificateStatus, revokedCertificates, crlShards, and more. Every other service reaches state only through the SA; nothing else opens a DB connection. That invariant is what lets Boulder run the CA in a network-isolated security zone.

tour.title: Validation Authority — challenges and MPIC
tour.description: va/va.go implements ACME challenge validation and enforces Multi-Perspective Issuance Corroboration (MPIC): the primary VA runs the challenge locally, then calls out to remote VA perspectives in diverse networks and requires a quorum of matching results before declaring success. This defends against localized BGP hijacks. http.go implements HTTP-01 (fetches /.well-known/acme-challenge/<token> from the identifier), dns.go implements DNS-01 and DNS-ACCOUNT-01 (looks for a TXT record under _acme-challenge.<identifier>), and bdns/dns.go is Boulder's own DNS resolver with DNSSEC validation, CAA lookup, and explicit handling of split-horizon and rebind attempts. The RA blocks on the VA's result before asking the CA to sign.

tour.title: Certificate Authority — signing, policy, and linting
tour.description: ca/ca.go holds the signing service; it never talks to the internet and receives requests only from the RA. issuance/issuer.go builds the tbsCertificate from the validated order, issuance/cert.go handles end-entity cert shape, and issuance/crl.go builds CRL templates. policy/pa.go is the Policy Authority — it enforces identifier-level rules (allowed character sets, reserved names, wildcard constraints, public-suffix handling) before an order is even accepted. Every candidate certificate is passed through linter/linter.go, a zlint-backed pre-flight check that rejects anything violating CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements or Mozilla/Chrome profiles. Nothing reaches an HSM without clearing the linter.

tour.title: Publisher and Certificate Transparency
tour.description: publisher/publisher.go submits issued precertificates to the configured CT logs and collects Signed Certificate Timestamps (SCTs). Boulder uses the precertificate mechanism defined in RFC 6962: the CA first signs a precert with a poison extension, the Publisher submits it to multiple CT logs, and only after an SCT quorum is returned does the CA issue the final certificate with those SCTs embedded. publisher.proto fixes the gRPC contract the RA uses to drive this. Without an SCT embedded in the final cert, modern browsers would reject it — so this step is load-bearing for every successful issuance.

tour.title: Revocation and the CRL pipeline
tour.description: Boulder publishes sharded CRLs so that revocation stays useful even as the issued-cert corpus grows into the billions. crl/updater/updater.go periodically scans the SA for revoked and about-to-expire certs, buckets them into deterministic shards, and asks the CA to sign each shard's CRL (using issuance/crl.go). crl/storer/storer.go then uploads the signed bytes to object storage (S3-compatible) where relying parties fetch them. Shards are stable: a given certificate's serial always maps to the same CRL URL across its lifetime, which is what the AIA extension embedded at issuance time points to.

tour.title: Rate limits, nonces, and feature flags
tour.description: ratelimits/limiter.go implements Boulder's Redis-backed rate limiter using the GCRA (Generic Cell Rate Algorithm) in gcra.go — the same token-bucket-equivalent that powers Let's Encrypt's public issuance caps. The WFE and RA consult the limiter before expensive operations (new-account, new-order, issuance, failed-validation). nonce/nonce.go is a standalone service that mints and redeems ACME replay nonces (the Replay-Nonce header on every response, the nonce claim in every signed JWS). features/features.go is the global feature-flag table — config-driven booleans that gate in-progress behavior so new code can ship dark and be enabled per-deployment without a rebuild.

tour.title: How Boulder builds, tests, and runs
tour.description: docker-compose.yml is the local dev substrate: it starts MariaDB, Redis (for rate limits and nonces), a consul-based service-discovery shim, a mock DNS server, and a container running the unified boulder binary in all-in-one mode so every service is reachable on localhost. The Makefile wraps common developer entry points (build, test, integration, lint, generate). .github/workflows/boulder-ci.yml is the upstream CI pipeline — it runs unit tests against multiple Go versions, integration tests via docker-compose, and the go-generate freshness check that catches out-of-date .pb.go files. Together these three files are how you take the code you just toured and actually exercise it end to end.

languageLesson.title: docker-compose for multi-service local dev
languageLesson.content: docker-compose.yml describes a stack of containers that share a network. Boulder's compose file declares services for MariaDB, Redis, a mock DNS challtestsrv, and the boulder binary itself, with `depends_on` ordering so the DB is ready before boulder starts. Named volumes persist the MariaDB data directory across restarts. `docker compose up` starts the whole graph; `docker compose exec boulder …` runs commands inside the main container. This is the fastest way to reproduce a bug against a real gRPC + MariaDB + Redis environment without touching production.
